title: PROFINET: Update DCP + PnSec dissectors to new pn specification
description:
The Imprint Private Key request has been removed from the PROFINET
specification. Drop the associated dissection glue that decoded a
2-byte length followed by the private-key blob, along with its two hf
entries (pn_io.private_key, pn_io.private_key_length) and the local
u16PrivateKeyLength scratch variable.

In the SecurityRequest_block dissector, delete the entire
`if (u16SecurityOperation == 0x0007)` branch. In the SecurityResponse_block
switch, remove the empty `case(0x0007)` fall-through label; the
remaining Imprint/Remove/SetSecurityMode responses (0x0008..0x000C) still
share the empty-body fall-through. Any future frame that surfaces with
0x0007 now falls through to the `default` case and is rendered via
dissect_pn_undecoded, which is the correct behavior for a reserved
opcode.

Mark 0x0007 as "Reserved" in the pn_io_security_operation range_string
so the SecurityOperation column no longer advertises the withdrawn
operation.

AI-Assisted: yes

notes.body: How about dissecting old capture files?

The Imprint of the private key was an interim solution and was never integrated into any productive profinet stacks. If you mean the NME renaming, I have to look for a solution to differentiate between versions. The BlockVersion situation is unclear.

@JaapKeuter I discussed the topic with one of our architects: He verified that the changes are fine regarding old captures, all changes are only affecting outdated developer versions, because the changed parts were never released officially.
added this merge request to the [merge train](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_trains) at position 5
